reviewedFor.g10:e-6: Provides the explicit subduction-to-magma-to-volcano causal link as supplemental reading on the effects above a descending plate.

reason: English, Tagalog and Cebuano describe one plate descending beneath another and magma supplying volcanoes; titles identify subduction. USGS confirms this outcome through fluid-assisted melting above the slab. The brief wording does not state that the whole slab melts; it is useful outcome-level reading, not a complete mechanism or earthquake explanation. No emphasis is present.

The English and Tagalog give useful variation, inheritance and reproductive-success conditions, and all emphasis spans match. Cebuano substitutes nagpanamkon og daghan for reproducing more: Binisaya identifies panamkon with pregnancy cravings and its root with conceiving. That does not reliably express differential reproduction across organisms. Hold both evolution placements pending lexical correction/review; titles themselves are aligned.

The English elastic-storage/rebound example could support both proposed lessons, but current translations leave the physical comparison uncertain: Tagalog namumukol does not unambiguously convey compression, and Cebuano lapok names mud where English specifies clay. Binisaya supports the mud sense (with a broad clay gloss), so this is a contextual uncertainty, not a global ban on lapok. The clipped phrase titles add no clarification. Hold for precise trilingual material/deformation wording; no emphasis is present.

The titles and matching momentum emphasis align in all languages, but every body says total momentum stays the same in a collision without defining an isolated system or negligible external impulse. This unconditional statement can mislead when external forces act. OpenStax explicitly requires zero net external force; hold the conservation lesson until that condition is present.

The English describes DNA-informed rice breeding, but Tagalog bigas and Cebuano bugas in the drought-survival clause can describe harvested/milled grains rather than living rice plants (the titles correctly use palay/humay). Binisaya explicitly lists milled rice/food grain for bugas. Hold this material referent ambiguity. Independently, g10:l-8 is not established: studying DNA for breeding does not explicitly identify genetic engineering, GMOs or IVF. DNA emphasis matches in all languages.

reviewedFor.g8:body-systems: The epiglottis directing swallowed food away from the airway is a concrete interaction between digestive and respiratory structures for the body-systems lesson.

reason: The English flap-over-larynx account is a suitable elementary simplification; Tagalog and Cebuano retain the protected airway and food route. Titles identify the swallowing cover rather than a different organ. No emphasis is present. Accept as one safe anatomical example; it supplies no model, simulation or excretion coverage.

reviewedFor.g9:f-4: Paddle pushing water backward and water pushing the banca forward explicitly illustrate equal, oppositely directed interaction forces.
reviewedFor.g9:f-5: The rowing example supplies a specific everyday action-reaction pair that students can subsequently represent with force arrows.

reason: All three bodies preserve the backward/forward directions and equal strength; titles identify rowing, and Newton-law emphasis matches each body. Treat the banca/paddle/rower as the connected rowing system; this is an age-appropriate concrete force example. Admission is reading support, not evidence that a diagram was drawn.

The endangered-turtle topic and matching organism emphasis are aligned across languages, but the card only says most endangered, not the explicit Critically Endangered classification needed by g9:l-6. The IUCN specialist account gives that category and describes adults as semi-aquatic in lowland forests; lives only in freshwater is too exclusive. Hold for both conservation-category precision and habitat scope rather than infer the missing classification.

English, Tagalog and Cebuano consistently offer only a few cm/year and a fingernail analogy, with no direction, reference frame or measured trench segment. A consulted USGS regional account reports roughly 10 cm/year plate convergence partitioned over multiple boundaries, which does not validate this particular trench rate. Hold the quantitative claim and proposed future-position lesson; the body cannot support a defensible archipelago projection. Titles are topic-aligned and no emphasis is present.

Titles and convection emphasis are aligned across all three languages, but each body characterizes mantle rock generally as almost melted and presents a simple upward/downward push as the plate-driving mechanism. USGS distinguishes solid mantle that flows over long times from small localized melt regions. Hold the material-state ambiguity before using it to explain plate-driving mechanisms; the card also omits the asthenosphere, slab pull and ridge push.

reviewedFor.g10:f-4: Directly links heavier/faster motion to greater momentum and greater stopping demand.
reviewedFor.g10:f-5: Provides the stopping comparison that a controlled mass/speed investigation can test.
reviewedFor.g10:f-6: Explicitly relates stopping momentum to either a larger force or a longer application time.

reason: All three bodies preserve the momentum, force and time relationship, with the ordinary comparison understood at otherwise comparable conditions. Titles are compressed but retain greater momentum and stopping difficulty; no emphasis is present. Safe conceptual reading, without claiming an investigation or quantitative calculation was performed.

reviewedFor.g8:kinetic-potential: The spring-like arm structure is a concrete biological example of stored elastic energy and subsequent movement.
reviewedFor.g8:energy-exchange: The stated storage followed by release into a rapid strike explicitly illustrates potential-to-kinetic transfer.

reason: Berkeley researchers directly report elastic energy storage and release in the mantis-shrimp appendage. The English/TL/BIS bodies and organism titles preserve that sequence; Cebuano kusog has an attested energy sense in the corpus, so unfamiliar vocabulary is not treated as an error. All emphasis spans match. A descriptive animal example, not an instruction to handle it.

reviewedFor.g8:land-sea-storms: Explicitly links landfall weakening to loss of the warm ocean energy supply.

reason: The three bodies retain the warm-ocean/landfall contrast. The English all its energy is a broad classroom shorthand for the ocean heat/moisture supply, not a claim that landfall ends danger. TL and BIS titles are compressed but remain about typhoons over land; there is no unmatched emphasis. Accept only for the energy-source contrast, not as a safety or post-landfall hazard account.

Current bodies discuss opposite momentum changes, not the equal opposite forces required by the only proposed lesson g9:f-4. That relationship is inferable but unstated, so the placement is too loose. English additionally claims total momentum is exactly unchanged without defining the rocket-plus-exhaust system or external-force condition; TL/BIS omit that conservation clause. Titles and emphasis match the momentum topic. Hold rather than import the missing force explanation.

reviewedFor.g10:e-1: Names GPS/satellites and the speed and direction measurements used to track tectonic motion.

reason: The three bodies and GPS titles faithfully retain the observing technology and measured motion. Exactly is colloquial precision rather than an offered uncertainty-free numeric datum. No emphasis is present; this is safe conceptual support for geodetic measurement, without claiming the student measured displacement.

All three bodies explicitly define tectonic plates as pieces of crust, omitting their rigid uppermost-mantle component. That is a consequential definition error in a plate-tectonics lesson. Titles and uplift outcome otherwise align, but the generic collision statement cannot justify carrying that inaccurate plate definition into g10:e-7. No emphasis is present.

Every language tells the child to switch off the main power first during an electrical fire, without an if-safe condition, adult help or evacuation priority. The no-water warning is useful, and titles/emphasis match, but the imperative can send a child toward hazardous equipment. USFA child guidance prioritizes leaving and staying out. Hold both safety placements until the current instruction is safe.

Titles and all three bodies consistently state force times duration, but omit that impulse uses constant force or the average net force when force varies. The word exactly makes this an unconditional formula claim. OpenStax states the constant-force assumption explicitly; hold the standalone definition until its condition is included. No emphasis is present.

reviewedFor.g9:f-1: The passenger continuing forward after the car stops is an explicit everyday inertia example.
reviewedFor.g10:f-6: The belt gradually reducing forward momentum provides a concrete force-over-stopping-time example.
reviewedFor.g10:f-7: Seatbelt restraint is directly identified as collision protection that reduces a hard impact.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain continued passenger motion and the restraining belt reducing it. Slowly is relative to the abrupt unrestrained impact, not a claim that crashes happen slowly. Titles and forward-momentum emphasis are aligned. Safe explanatory reading; it does not quantify force or replace proper restraint instructions.

The three bodies say growth stays fast until the population hits the limit and only then slows. Logistic growth instead slows while approaching carrying capacity as resources become limiting. That timing is the precise learning point of g10:l-11, so this is not merely omitted detail. Titles and population emphasis align, but the science requires correction.

reviewedFor.g10:m-9: A burning flame explicitly illustrates chemical changes releasing energy as heat/light, supporting the exothermic side of the lesson.

reason: The qualified many chemical changes avoids claiming all reactions release heat. English, Tagalog and Cebuano retain release and heat/light; energy emphasis matches and titles are consistent. Safe descriptive example only, with no flame experiment instruction and no claim to teach endothermic reactions.

The English heat-to-steam electricity concept is potentially useful, but Tagalog binabarena tayo and Cebuano ginabarena ta make us the entity being drilled rather than clearly expressing that people drill. Corpus search finds only this card for both constructions. Hold the actor ambiguity and blanket safely assurance; no device chain is explained. The proposed g10:f-13 placement is also weak because the text supplies no renewable/nonrenewable comparison or environmental impact. Titles and emphasis are otherwise aligned.

reviewedFor.g8:crust-sources: Identifies the crust as the thin outer solid-rock layer, a direct starting fact for investigating continental and oceanic crust.

reason: English accurately includes land, mountains and ocean floor; TL/BIS shorten to the outer solid layer where people live without contradicting that account. Titles identify crust and no emphasis is present. Accept only as introductory layer reading, not as a complete oceanic/continental comparison or sourced research activity.

Each body makes the same unqualified same-group/same-outer-electron-count assertion. Helium has two valence electrons while other group-18 elements have eight, and transition groups need further care. The proposed lesson explicitly includes exceptions, so this standalone rule is misleading without a main-group qualification and helium exception. Titles are aligned and no emphasis is present.

reviewedFor.g8:land-water: Provides the directly relevant approximate seven-tenths water coverage of Earth surface.

reason: The English surface proportion is correct at this precision; TL/BIS retain the seven-in-ten quantity and ocean-cover context, making clear this concerns surface coverage. Titles are compressed but identify the ocean/blue-planet idea, and no emphasis is present. A suitable numerical reading example.

reviewedFor.g8:tidal-energy: Explicitly identifies rising/falling tides as a source of renewable electricity; waves provide a second ocean-energy example.

reason: English, Tagalog and Cebuano preserve tidal/wave motion and electricity, with correctly matching tides emphasis. The renewable explanation is brief but does not promise unlimited output. Titles refer to ocean energy. Accept introductory generation reading; it does not assess tidal range or a particular site.

reviewedFor.g9:f-2: Relates net-force direction to speeding up, slowing down and turning, directly supporting acceleration as a speed/direction change.

reason: All three bodies preserve the distinction between net-force direction and motion changes. Forward/backward are ordinary motion-relative directions in the example; no contrary coordinate frame is supplied. Titles and net-force emphasis align. Safe supplemental conceptual reading without claiming a practical demonstration.

English/TL and the opening Cebuano clause correctly distinguish beneficial, harmful and neutral outcomes. The final Cebuano walay bali is uncertain in this neutrality sense: the corpus has only this body for that phrase and other bali uses concern breaks/bending; the attempted dictionary lookup yielded no accessible definition. This is a lexical hold, not a proven global false-friend claim. Titles are aligned and no emphasis exists; do not admit until that current phrase is resolved.

reviewedFor.g9:m-2: The tightly joined nitrogen atoms being separated and new substances forming is a concrete example of bond breaking and chemical change.

reason: NASA NTRS explicitly describes the large energy needed to break the nitrogen-nitrogen bond and lightning as an abiotic mechanism. The card speaks of atoms stuck together, not nuclear splitting; TL/BIS retain separation and new-substance formation. Titles remain about lightning and atmospheric nitrogen; no emphasis exists. It omits later oxidation/rain chemistry, so admission is only the bond-change example.

Every body says predators keep prey close to carrying capacity. Predation can regulate prey well below the resource-limited carrying capacity, so that near-capacity outcome is not a general consequence. Titles and carrying-capacity emphasis are aligned, but this misleading ecology rule should not support g10:l-10; the card also does not specify food, water, shelter or mates as limiting resources.

reviewedFor.g10:l-1: Sweating and widening skin vessels give specific physiological responses that reduce excess body temperature.
reviewedFor.g10:l-2: The heat-triggered response that opposes the initial temperature rise is an explicit everyday negative-feedback example.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain both sweating and skin-vessel dilation and their cooling outcome; titles and sweat emphasis match. The heat-loss physiology is correct as a short account in ordinary warm conditions. It does not claim to teach the sensor/control center or positive feedback.

The three bodies incorrectly explain any nonzero net force as one force being stronger than the others. Equal forces in different non-opposite directions can have a nonzero vector sum. This is a definition error, not just a missing example. Titles and unbalanced-forces emphasis match, but hold the net-force lesson until the scalar stronger-force shortcut is removed.

All three bodies make a strong undersea earthquake sufficient to create a tsunami while omitting sudden water displacement. NOAA explicitly says not all earthquakes cause tsunamis and identifies seafloor displacement as the mechanism. This is the proposed lesson's central distinction, so the force/energy-only explanation is inadequate and potentially misleading. Titles are aligned; no emphasis exists.

The work formula is unconditional force times distance in all languages; it omits the component of force along displacement and cannot handle perpendicular forces or negative work. The proposed lesson explicitly includes direction. Titles and work emphasis align, but the central formula needs its parallel-force condition before use.

The annual debris-crossing mechanism is broadly correct, but every language attributes both Perseids and Geminids to comet dust. NASA identifies the Geminids' parent as asteroid 3200 Phaethon. Titles and emphasis are aligned; hold the false named example instead of relying on its otherwise useful annual timing.

reviewedFor.g10:f-4: Explicit p = mv and the fast heavy truck connect mass, velocity and the difficulty of stopping momentum.

reason: All three bodies preserve the correct momentum formula and truck comparison; titles carry the same formula and example. No emphasis is present. Heavy/fast is an ordinary otherwise-comparable contrast, and the card gives no risky stopping experiment. Useful direct supplemental reading.

The English/TL/BIS bodies all say chloroplasts occur only in plant cells. Photosynthetic protists also have chloroplasts, as OpenStax explicitly describes; only is therefore false in the unqualified current claim. The sunlight/photosynthesis role, titles and matching emphasis are otherwise aligned. Hold rather than teach an incorrect exclusivity rule.

reviewedFor.g8:mechanical-energy: States directly that mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic and potential energy.

reason: English, Tagalog and Cebuano retain both energy terms and the sum relationship. The Cebuano short title uses the corpus-attested broad energy sense of kusog, while its body supplies the precise English science term. No emphasis is present. Correct definition-level reading; it does not add a work calculation.

reviewedFor.g8:periodic-history: Identifies Mendeleev, 1869 and grouping by similar properties as a specific historical contribution.

reason: Although the opening question says first table, each answer qualifies it as the first widely used one, avoiding a claim that no predecessor existed. All three languages retain the date, scientist and property grouping; titles/emphasis identify him. The RSC history confirms his 1869 organization and preceding developments.

The Atlantic seafloor-spreading example is useful, but all languages open with a general statement that our oceans are growing; ocean basins do not all widen. The title also shifts the growth to the ridges rather than clearly the spreading basin. Hold this scope ambiguity. g8:plates-crust additionally lacks a link from crust to lithospheric plate composition; g10:e-2 has a plausible divergent-boundary example but it does not override the current wording problem. No emphasis is present.

reviewedFor.g8:volcano-types: Directly distinguishes active, dormant and extinct activity descriptions, with Taal and Mayon as familiar active examples.

reason: All three languages retain ability to erupt again and the qualified unlikely for extinct volcanoes; the sleeping metaphor is immediately explained. Titles and three-types emphasis agree. Accept as a common classroom activity scheme, not as the sole agency classification or a prediction of imminent eruption.

reviewedFor.g9:f-9: Separate current paths and other lamps continuing after one goes out give a direct practical advantage of parallel wiring.

reason: The English/TL/BIS explanations retain branch independence under the ordinary open-lamp failure example. Titles and separate-path emphasis align. Safe conceptual reading; no household-wiring procedure or claim about short-circuit failure is made.

reviewedFor.g9:l-5: Connects species variety to some species surviving difficult conditions and sustaining ecosystem functioning.

reason: The English uses likely rather than guaranteeing survival, and the translations preserve the multiple-species/resilience idea without promising total immunity to disturbance. Titles and biodiversity emphasis match. A suitable qualitative resilience example, not a claim that every species can replace every other.

reviewedFor.g9:m-1: Limewater becoming cloudy supplies the concrete indicator used in a carbon-dioxide/new-substance investigation.
reviewedFor.g10:m-1: The iodine color change and cloudy limewater explicitly illustrate visible reaction indicators.

reason: The three bodies accurately retain iodine-starch blue-black coloration and the carbon-dioxide limewater test; titles/emphasis match. The instructions name ordinary classroom tests without ingestion, heating or dangerous quantities. Accept as reading about observed test results; it does not supply control/repeat procedures or credit a completed investigation.

The simplified different-sized-atom account can explain strengthening in some alloys, but every body generalizes that an alloy becomes harder to bend or break; hardness, strength and brittleness are not interchangeable across alloys. More decisively for g9:m-10, the card supplies neither the sea-of-electrons bonding model nor electrical/thermal conduction. Titles are aligned and no emphasis exists. Hold rather than use a loose all-metals association.

The cubic sodium-chloride lattice is correct, but each body promises that every visible salt grain is a cube. Ground, fractured or differently grown salt crystals need not be perfect cubes; the proposed microscope observation can directly contradict the claim. Titles and CUBE emphasis amplify this overstatement. Hold until crystal structure is distinguished from every grain's external shape.

All three bodies generalize to cave animals and give energy saving as the definitive cause of eye reduction. Research on cavefish discusses multiple genetic/selection mechanisms and population differences, so this needs a qualified organism-specific account rather than purposeful eyes-shrank-to-save-energy wording. TL/BIS also move from tiny eyes to eyes disappearing. The titles do not resolve the overgeneralization; no emphasis exists.

reviewedFor.g10:m-3: Nitrogen and oxygen combining to make nitrogen oxides is an explicit synthesis/combination example.

reason: The three bodies preserve both reactants and the oxide product; heat pushing together is a simple activation metaphor rather than a nuclear process. Cebuano mixing is clarified by formation of the named new substance. Titles identify fixation and all oxide emphasis spans match. The lightning chemistry is supported by the consulted nitrogen-fixation account.

All bodies promise exactly salt and water whenever any acid meets any base. That requires qualification to the intended hydroxide-neutralization cases; bases such as ammonia can form a salt with acid without producing water. Titles and emphasized word equation preserve the same overgeneralization. Hold before using this as a general word-equation recipe in g10:m-5.

reviewedFor.g10:m-6: The burning-wood example explicitly counts ash plus gases against wood plus the consumed air, illustrating conserved total matter in a reaction.

reason: All three bodies retain both gaseous products and air reactant, avoiding the common apparent-mass-loss error. TL/BIS use everyday weight vocabulary in the same-location comparison while English states mass; the full bodies make the accounting meaning of the conservation titles clear. Emphasis matches. Accept only the chemical-reaction context, not a universal claim about nuclear mass-energy conversion or a burn experiment.

reviewedFor.g10:m-6: Equal counts of each atomic kind on both sides explicitly represent conservation through a chemical rearrangement.
reviewedFor.g10:m-7: Explains the atom-count goal of balancing a chemical equation.

reason: All three bodies and balance titles preserve equal atom counts and mass conservation; emphasis matches. Proves is read as demonstrates in the symbolic model, not an experimental proof of the law. This is correct purpose-level reading without claiming coefficients or a worked balancing procedure.

The moles-per-litre-of-solution definition is scientifically correct and all titles/emphasis align, but the proposed Grade 7 lesson measures solute against a stated solvent volume. Solution volume is a different denominator, and the card introduces moles without its prerequisite. Hold this exact placement rather than substitute an advanced concentration metric for the supplied lesson target.

The approximate six-month polar day/night and tilt explanation is suitable science at the poles, and titles/emphasis align. However, the Cebuano sequence uses unay where English says then. The corpus has no independent temporal use; Binisaya defines unay with accessible/attached/mainland/self-inflict senses, not the required transition. Hold this unresolved current-copy error rather than silently reading a corrected conjunction.

reviewedFor.g7:heat-temperature: Contrasts equal object temperature with different sensations of cold, providing a useful prompt for distinguishing temperature from heat transfer.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain the same-room, same-temperature comparison and metal/wood titles; emphasis matches. This is the conventional equilibrated-room example, with the equilibrium assumption implicit. It deliberately stops before the conductivity explanation, so accept only as the concrete contrast, not a complete answer to why.

All three bodies and titles accurately identify FaultFinder's intended active-fault proximity function, and emphasis matches. Current PHIVOLCS evidence, however, says FaultFinder is unavailable for security work and directs users to HazardHunterPH. Its capability page also describes mapped proximity, not the English promise of an exact house/school fault distance. Hold current availability/precision until copy is reconciled with the official service state.

reviewedFor.g7:one-many-cells: Identifies bacteria as cellular living units and contrasts them with noncellular viruses, a concrete support for recognizing single-celled organisms.

reason: English, Tagalog and Cebuano retain the cell/noncell contrast, and the titles identify the compared groups. CDC confirms antibiotics do not work on viruses; the card says can kill bacteria rather than all bacteria are susceptible. It offers no medication-taking instruction. Accept only the bacterial-cell distinction, not a full explanation of antibiotic targets or multicellular organization.

All three bodies change no fixed shape into water with no shape at all. Liquids have a shape set by their container; the state change removes a fixed shape rather than shape itself. The particle loosening language and titles reinforce an incomplete account without energy transfer. Hold the central state-property error; no emphasis exists.

The three bodies restrict the definition of fragmentation to two parts, though fragmentation can yield more than two. The capability/large-enough qualifications are useful and the title/emphasis match, but the definition needs correction before the example supports asexual reproduction. It also does not explicitly discuss offspring genetic similarity; no procedure should be inferred from the body.

All languages correctly qualify ten percent as approximate, but then assign all remaining energy to activity/respiration/heat. Energy also remains in uneaten or unassimilated biomass and enters detrital pathways. Hold this overly exhaustive remainder account. g7:trophic-levels also has no producer/consumer/pyramid identification; g7:energy-transfer is a clear intended fit once the energy accounting is sound. Titles align and no emphasis exists.

The current question and answers describe rapidly moving electrons arranged in surrounding layers without saying this is a shell/energy-level model rather than a physical electron path. TL umiikot and BIS naglibot strengthen the orbit reading. The proposed lesson explicitly guards against exact shell paths. Titles and emphasis match, but hold until the model limitation is explicit enough not to teach a miniature planetary trajectory.

reviewedFor.g8:kinetic-potential: Contrasts maximum potential energy at the turning point with fastest motion/kinetic energy at the bottom.
reviewedFor.g8:energy-exchange: Explicitly states that stored potential energy becomes kinetic energy on the downward swing.
reviewedFor.g8:falling-energy: The descending pendulum is a gravity-driven example in which loss of height corresponds to increased kinetic energy.

reason: All three bodies preserve the turning-point pause and lowest-point speed maximum of an ordinary pendulum. Titles and kinetic-energy emphasis agree. The idealized energy exchange is accurate without a perpetual-motion claim; it does not cover damping or quantitative energy losses.

The body's stratospheric ozone/UV-protection account is sound in all three languages and emphasis matches. Tagalog title Sapot ng Osono, however, uses the web sense where the English and Cebuano name a layer. Corpus review found 23 Tagalog body uses of sapot, with the inspected contexts consistently spider-web material, not atmospheric layer. Hold this title-sense uncertainty rather than promote a misleading title on a radiation lesson.

reviewedFor.g9:f-3: For fixed mass, doubled force and doubled acceleration plus F = ma provide the explicit relationship for a controlled force investigation.

reason: The three bodies preserve the fixed-mass condition and formula; the formula is the standard resultant-force Newton model. Titles use ordinary force/acceleration wording and proportionality emphasis matches. Safe conceptual reading only; no investigation data or procedure is claimed.

UV exposure, DNA damage and later skin-cancer risk are real, but English title Sunburn Is UV DNA Damage and all bodies identify DNA damage as the direct acute sunburn mechanism. The 2024 Molecular Cell study and its 2025 university report identify RNA-damage/ribotoxic response as the acute driver. Hold this mechanistic oversimplification; the cancer-risk warning remains valid. TL/BIS preserve the same causal claim; no emphasis exists.

reviewedFor.g9:m-6: Sodium chloride is a specific binary ionic example illustrating cation/metal first and anion ending -ide.

reason: All three bodies explicitly use the same simple metal/nonmetal naming pattern and sodium-chloride example. The compressed titles refer to ionic naming; no emphasis exists. Accept within this binary example, not as coverage of polyatomic ions, variable-charge metals or formula writing.

The electron-sharing water example and matching body emphasis are scientifically suitable, but TL/BIS title Kobalenteng Bono has unresolved bond terminology. The corpus has four chemical-body uses in Tagalog but zero in Cebuano; the attempted Cebuano dictionary lookup did not supply a definition. Since the corpus itself can propagate generator errors, hold the unsupported Cebuano title sense pending lexical review, without claiming all uses of bono are wrong.

reviewedFor.g9:m-8: Directly connects the formula H₂O to water and its two hydrogen/one oxygen atom composition.

reason: All three bodies retain the exact 2:1 atom count, molecule unit and formula; titles and H₂O emphasis agree. Stuck together is an age-appropriate bond simplification. Correct, safe named-compound reading, without claiming coverage of carbon dioxide or ammonia.

reviewedFor.g7:particle-model: Explicitly says matter is composed of tiny atoms/molecules.
reviewedFor.g7:particle-motion: Describes continuing particle motion and differing separations in familiar states.
reviewedFor.g7:particle-diagrams: Packed vibrating solids, sliding nearby liquid particles and separated moving gas particles supply the distinctions a state diagram represents.

reason: English/TL/BIS preserve the three-state particle comparisons. Tight/close/far is a suitable simple model for ordinary substances, not a quantitative packing law. Titles identify the particulate nature of matter; no emphasis exists. Accept introductory readings only, with no claim to demonstrate diagrams, purity or the temperature dependence of motion.

The typical large plant central vacuole/smaller animal vacuole contrast is useful, but all bodies turn it into a universal just-one-permanent versus many-temporary rule. FSU describes many plant cells and animal vacuoles tending to be smaller, appropriately qualifying these variable organelles. Titles and emphasis match. Hold the unqualified cell-type rule until typical cells are distinguished from all cells.

reviewedFor.g9:e-3: The ridge forms where plates pull apart and erupted material solidifies, a direct divergent-boundary example.
reviewedFor.g10:e-2: Combines divergent motion, new rock and the ridge structure, explicitly illustrating a plate-boundary process and landform.

reason: All three bodies retain underwater location, plate separation and lava hardening; titles/emphasis agree. The global mid-ocean ridge system is correctly identified as the longest mountain chain. Do not add g8:global-patterns: this single feature does not explain how distributions of active belts relate to oceanic versus continental crust.

reviewedFor.g8:inheritance-ratios: States the expected 1:2:1 genotype probabilities for a simple heterozygote-by-heterozygote cross.

reason: English/TL/BIS distinguish homozygous dominant, heterozygous and homozygous recessive outcomes and describe chances rather than a guaranteed four-child family. The one-gene context is the standard simple Mendelian model; titles and ratio emphasis match. Age-appropriate genetics reading, without claiming phenotype ratios or a drawn Punnett square.

reviewedFor.g8:local-motion: A banked road curve is a local circular-motion example with the required inward turning force.

reason: All three bodies retain a tilted road and inward centripetal contribution. This is a simplified description of the inward component of road contact force, not a separate newly invented force. Titles are compressed but identify the curve. No emphasis exists, and the card gives no driving-speed instruction or guarantee that all banked turns are safe.

reviewedFor.g9:e-7: Returning/reflected seismic waves from earthquakes are explicitly used to infer deep Earth structure.

reason: English names layer boundaries; TL/BIS shorten the account to bouncing/returning waves and the inferred interior, without contradicting it. Seismic reflection is a real method, though it is only one of the seismic clues. Titles and emphasis match. Accept for interior inference, not coverage of P/S-wave phase differences.

reviewedFor.g9:f-8: Names an ammeter, amperes and inserting the meter into the current path, directly supporting meter placement in a circuit.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain the instrument and its series-path connection. How much flows is colloquial current rather than a charge-total formula; the ampere unit anchors it. Titles and ammeter emphasis align. Conceptual circuit reading only, with no mains-testing directions or claim that a full circuit was assembled.

reviewedFor.g10:e-2: Separating plates, rising magma and newly cooled crust explicitly describe a divergent boundary.

reason: All three bodies preserve the separation/rise/cooling sequence and the qualified usually on the ocean floor, allowing continental rifts. Titles describe new ocean crust; no emphasis exists. Correct, safe example-level plate-boundary reading.

Each body makes horizontal speed constant for projectile motion without the necessary negligible-air-resistance/other-horizontal-force assumption. It also labels the vertical component downward even during an upward launch. Titles and projectile emphasis match, but the unconditional rule is unsuitable for the everyday-projectile investigation lesson until the ideal model is stated.

The three bodies correctly recommend turning off unused electrical loads and give cost/environment benefits. Tagalog title Pag-iipon ng Kuryente, however, can describe accumulating/storing electricity rather than reducing use. Both independent corpus body uses of pag-iipon concern accumulating rainwater or dirty water. Hold this unresolved title sense; Cebuano pagtipig is not flagged, since its saving sense is attested. No emphasis exists.

All three bodies faithfully describe a familiar baking-soda/vinegar toy and matching chemical emphasis, but the proposed scientific-model lesson targets explaining unseen phenomena and model limitations. This card only says the toy looks like an eruption and supplies no real-volcano relationship or limit; its chemistry is not the volcanic process. Hold the loose model-label placement rather than credit unseen-process understanding.

The current claim is about dissolution speed, consistently translated with matching faster-dissolving emphasis. The proposed lesson concerns solubility/saturation, the amount that can dissolve at equilibrium. Faster is not more soluble, so admitting this card would blur the exact distinction under study. Titles are aligned; hold placement rather than treat the shared temperature keyword as sufficient.

reviewedFor.g8:acceleration: Free fall without air resistance gives an explicit equal-acceleration example despite different masses.
reviewedFor.g9:f-3: Connects larger mass to both larger gravitational force and inertia using F = ma, illustrating why acceleration remains the same.

reason: All three bodies preserve the crucial no-air-resistance condition and mass/weight/inertia contrast. The ordinary same-location fall is the context; titles are broader than the body but the body supplies its condition. No emphasis exists. Safe explanatory reading with no dropping-object activity instruction.

The three bodies state that noble gases are completely unreactive. Xenon and other heavier noble gases can form compounds, so a full valence shell explains low usual reactivity rather than absolute impossibility. Titles align but intensify the full-shell rule; no emphasis exists. Hold all three placements rather than teaching the incorrect absolute.

All three languages attach the two-allele rule to most traits rather than to a diploid autosomal gene/locus. Many human traits are polygenic, so most traits do not correspond to just two inherited alleles. The one-from-each-parent idea would fit g7:inherited-information after that qualification; g8:inheritance-patterns also has no dominant/recessive or multigeneration pattern. Titles share the same oversimplification and no emphasis exists.

reviewedFor.g9:e-5: Names isotopic/radioactive dating as a way of obtaining numerical ages over geological timescales, directly supporting absolute dating.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain isotopic dating and ages in millions of years; titles are aligned and no emphasis exists. Smithsonian explains radiometric ages of fossil-bearing contexts, often via associated volcanic rocks. The card does not explicitly claim every fossil can be directly assayed, so accept this broad numeric-age introduction; it does not teach method choice, uncertainty or relative dating.

reviewedFor.g10:e-8: Repeated warm-ocean coral bleaching provides a stated ecological sign of warming rather than merely naming climate change.
reviewedFor.g10:e-11: Explicitly locates heat-related reef damage in the Philippines, supplying a local climate-impact example.

reason: NOAA identifies climate-driven ocean warming as the leading bleaching cause and documents Philippine bleaching reports. The three bodies retain the repeated heat/bleaching link and local setting; titles align and no emphasis exists. Accept impact/evidence reading only, not an attribution of every bleaching event solely to climate or a mitigation plan.

reviewedFor.g10:e-8: Increasing bleaching frequency is explicitly linked to warming oceans, a concrete ecological climate-change indicator.

reason: All three languages preserve warming and more frequent bleaching; masubsob corresponds to more frequent in the corpus usage rather than a different causal claim. Titles are aligned and no emphasis exists. NOAA supports the warming/bleaching mechanism; accept the qualitative trend example without claiming a measured local time series.

reviewedFor.g10:f-9: The transformer raising voltage for transmission and lowering it before homes is the specific distribution-stage function under study.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain both step-up and step-down functions and their sequence. The household grid context supplies ordinary AC use; the card does not claim transformer operation on steady DC. Titles align and no emphasis exists. Safe conceptual reading with no high-voltage handling instruction.

reviewedFor.g10:l-6: Growing viruses in eggs or laboratory cells to make a vaccine is an explicit biological-process/product example.
reviewedFor.g10:l-8: Laboratory cell culture for vaccine production is a concrete modern biotechnology process, without implying it must involve a GMO.

reason: CDC confirms egg-based and cell-culture vaccine production. All three bodies qualify some vaccines and retain growth then purification/processing; the English title is clarified by the body identifying the virus as what grows. No emphasis exists. Accept descriptive industrial biology, not vaccine preparation instructions or a claim that purification alone is a complete manufacturing protocol.

reviewedFor.g7:fault-types: Identifies the Philippine Fault as strike-slip and describes side-by-side horizontal movement.
reviewedFor.g7:fault-models: The familiar Philippine example links sudden sideways slip to an earthquake and supplies a hand-motion analogy for a model.

reason: PHIVOLCS confirms the Philippine Fault is a left-lateral strike-slip fault with major earthquake history. The three bodies preserve sideways sliding and sudden slip; the hand-rubbing comparison is only an analogy, not an earthquake experiment. Titles align and no emphasis exists. Accept the strike-slip example, without normal/reverse or fault-angle coverage.

All three bodies explicitly claim copper atoms are not chemically bonded. Metallic bonding is what holds the copper solid together; copper is an element because it contains one atomic/proton-number type, not because bonding is absent. Titles and element emphasis match, but the causal explanation is false and must not enter g8:pure-substances.

reviewedFor.g8:volcano-types: Gentle versus explosive eruption behavior is an explicit comparison of volcano behavior, with Mayon as a named example.

reason: All bodies retain contrasting eruption violence and Mayon's cone; TL/BIS omit the runny/thick lava distinction, so do not admit g8:volcano-shape, which needs the composition-to-shape relationship. The nearly/perfect-cone wording is an ordinary morphology description. Titles and difference emphasis align; accept only eruption-type reading.

reviewedFor.g9:e-3: A trench where plates converge and one descends directly illustrates a subduction boundary.
reviewedFor.g10:e-2: Connects convergent plate motion and descent to the trench landform.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain two plates coming together and one beneath the other; titles use trench/channel vocabulary in explicit ocean context, and plate emphasis matches. The simplified crash metaphor is immediately explained by subduction. Safe and directly relevant boundary reading.

reviewedFor.g9:f-12: Glass fibers carrying light signals for internet/telecommunications are an explicit practical electromagnetic-wave application.

reason: All three bodies retain fibers, light signals and long-distance communication; TL/BIS omit minimal loss without changing the mechanism. Titles are aligned and no emphasis exists. The text does not mistake light for electric current; suitable technology reading even though it does not cover the radio/X-ray/gamma examples.

reviewedFor.g9:m-5: Metal electron loss and nonmetal electron gain supply the explicit transfer step in the common ionic-bond model.

reason: English tend and the TL/BIS tendency/ease phrasing describe the standard elementary metal/nonmetal case, without claiming every pair will react. Titles and ionic-bond emphasis agree. Accept the electron-transfer component only; charged-ion attraction and a worked sodium/chlorine example are not supplied.

TL pagpapalala and BIS pagpalala replace fermenting with a worsening sense; the Cebuano corpus uses the root in worsening floods/erosion, and no independent fermentation sense was found. The Cebuano title also has an unresolved Ilang phrase instead of rice wine. DOST identifies the tapuy starter as bubod/binukbok, so the asserted tapay name needs local sourcing. Hold science/translation identity before considering the fermentation placement; no emphasis exists.

All three bodies and emphasis preserve the proposed mouth-color reaction, but the card presents chewing areca/betel nut with lime as a child-facing chemistry curiosity without any hazard context. IARC identifies areca/betel-quid chewing as carcinogenic. Hold age suitability of this standalone oral-exposure example and the insufficiently identified color-reaction claim; do not treat its mention of color as enough for g10:m-1.

reviewedFor.g7:earthquake-plan: Connects Philippine school drills to practicing the duck/cover/hold protective response during shaking.

reason: PHIVOLCS documents the drill technique and school-drill program. English/TL/BIS preserve the practice setting and three actions, with hiding understood as taking cover in that mnemonic. Titles/emphasis match. Accept preparation reading only; it supplies neither the complete physical technique nor a local evacuation/aftershock plan.

reviewedFor.g8:atomic-timeline: Rutherford and the discovery of the dense atomic nucleus provide one specific historical atomic-model milestone.

reason: All three bodies correctly associate Rutherford with the nucleus and place it at the atom's center. Cebuano baga is a broad dense/thick rendering, with nucleus providing the technical referent. Titles align and no emphasis exists. The repetitive question/answer is not a factual defect; accept one milestone, not a completed historical timeline.

Full/new-moon spring-tide flooding is a useful example, but all languages imply that other days are neap tides. Neap tides occur around the quarter phases, with intermediate tidal ranges between those extrema. The binary schedule is too loose for g8:tide-motions; titles and spring-tide emphasis otherwise match. Hold the phase/range account.

reviewedFor.g9:f-1: Explicitly gives zero total force as the condition for straight, constant-speed motion and says force changes motion.

reason: English/TL/BIS preserve the net-zero condition, straight direction and constant speed. Titles and Newton-law emphasis agree. The hockey-puck example is an appropriate low-friction illustration with the ideal condition explicitly stated. Correct and safe explanatory reading.

reviewedFor.g10:m-4: Acidic food taking up iron from an iron pan provides a concrete everyday acid–metal interaction.

reason: Primary cooking studies confirm iron transfer depends on acidity and other cooking conditions. English/TL/BIS say can add a small amount rather than prescribe a dose or claim treatment; titles/emphasis align. Old is incidental and does not assert old pans are uniquely effective. Accept ordinary cooking chemistry, not advice to use rusted/damaged cookware or treat iron deficiency.

All three bodies call a decreasing distance-time trace a return toward the start. Accumulated distance cannot decrease; this would require a position/displacement or explicitly distance-from-origin axis. Even distance from origin alone cannot identify a unique direction. The proposed lesson specifically warns that the graph alone does not show direction. Titles/emphasis match the mistaken rule; hold.

reviewedFor.g8:typhoon-formation: Warm ocean moisture rising and condensing, releasing storm energy, gives a specific part of tropical-cyclone formation.

reason: The English warm moist air and TL/BIS vapor descriptions preserve ascent, cooling/cloud formation and energy release into the rotating storm. Titles align and no emphasis exists. Accept the moisture/latent-heat mechanism as partial formation reading, not a claim that warm water alone guarantees a typhoon or that all formation conditions are covered.

The continental-origin statement is broadly relevant geology, but every language attributes modern Palawan–Borneo animal resemblance directly to Palawan drifting from Asia. Primary vertebrate research instead examines later Pleistocene land-bridge/colonization history; the card supplies no fossil, rock or tectonic chronology to establish that causal shortcut. Hold both the causal claim and loose continental-drift evidence placement. Titles align and no emphasis exists.

reviewedFor.g9:m-11: Good electrical conductivity explains the use of metals in wires, a concrete material-property example.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain easy electrical conduction and its wiring use. The title/body refer to electrical wire, so optical fibers are not a counterexample to the intended context. No emphasis exists. Correct qualitative reading; it does not provide the bonding model, a comparative measurement or other material properties.

reviewedFor.g9:m-3: Carbon supplies an explicit four-valence-electron example tied to its electron configuration.

reason: The 1s2 2s2 2p2 count, four outer electrons and group 14 placement are correct and identical in meaning across languages. Plain-text exponents remain readable in this notation; titles/emphasis match. Accept a concrete valence example, not a complete explanation of how those electrons form bonds.

English qualifies strongest shaking with usually, but Tagalog and Cebuano remove that qualification and assert maximum shaking at the epicenter. Local ground conditions, rupture geometry and distance can move the strongest shaking elsewhere. The epicenter is specifically above the focus, not defined by shaking strength. Titles align; no emphasis exists. Hold the cross-language certainty increase in this earthquake lesson.

reviewedFor.g7:inherited-information: Meiosis producing sperm/egg gametes identifies the reproductive cell process needed before information from two parents combines.

reason: The three bodies retain special cell division and sperm/egg examples, making the intended animal/human context clear. Titles and meiosis emphasis match. This is age-appropriate reproductive science and not sexual instruction. Accept only this process-identification component, not chromosome halving, fertilization or plant life-cycle coverage.

reviewedFor.g7:sun-atmosphere: Explains that much solar light passes through the atmosphere and is absorbed by Earth surface.

reason: English/TL/BIS preserve mostly/much rather than declaring the atmosphere completely transparent. First absorbed refers to the transmitted portion that reaches the surface, not to all solar radiation. Titles use a clear-window analogy and transparent emphasis matches. Accept the transmission/surface-absorption component, without reflection/scattering coverage.

reviewedFor.g8:community-support: PAGASA storm-surge warnings are a concrete official service alerting coastal communities before a typhoon.

reason: PAGASA documents the warning product and coastal hazard purpose. All three bodies preserve agency, warning and before-arrival protection; titles/emphasis match. Keep safe expresses the warning's purpose, not a guarantee of no harm. Accept awareness reading, without supplying a local evacuation plan.

reviewedFor.g8:energy-exchange: Elevated water stores energy that is released into falling water, a concrete potential-to-motion example.
reviewedFor.g8:hydropower: Reservoir storage and release through a turbine describe the specific energy stage used in dam hydropower.

reason: All three bodies retain elevated water and the turbine release path. Battery is explicitly an analogy, not a chemical claim; the body anchors storage in height. Titles are compressed but aligned and no emphasis exists. Accept the generic dam mechanism; it does not name a Philippine station or describe the generator/electric distribution stage.

reviewedFor.g8:power: Defines watt as joule per second, explicitly linking the power unit to an energy-transfer rate.

reason: English/TL/BIS preserve one joule each second and symbol W; titles repeat the same correct relationship. Energy produced is ordinary output/conversion language here, not a claim to create energy from nothing. No emphasis exists. Correct unit/rate reading without a work-rate calculation.

reviewedFor.g9:e-4: Relates fossil resemblance to the relative ages of successive rock layers, supplying fossil-succession evidence useful in dating strata.
reviewedFor.g10:l-5: Different older forms and greater resemblance in newer forms provide a concrete fossil-record pattern consistent with change over time.

reason: The body uses usually/often rather than an absolute every-fossil claim in the English/TL. Initial concern about BIS kanunay was checked against Binisaya, which explicitly includes an often/frequent sense as well as always; it is not a proven certainty error here. Titles and fossil emphasis agree. Accept the ordinary undisturbed-layer example, not an index-fossil procedure.

reviewedFor.g9:l-8: Nursery growth followed by transplantation identifies a specific reef-restoration method that can inform conservation research.

reason: NOAA describes the same nursery/outplanting approach. All three bodies retain that sequence, and titles/emphasis align. Helps heal is a simple restoration aim, not a survival guarantee. The text describes conservation work without instructing a child to break or collect wild coral. Accept the method example, without claiming a researched Philippine project.

reviewedFor.g7:solute-solvent: Ether is an explicit example of a liquid solvent that dissolves other substances.

reason: PubChem identifies diethyl ether as both solvent and refrigerant; the museum's documented ether refrigeration machine corroborates the ancillary cooling use. English/TL/BIS and ether emphasis preserve the same two uses, with aligned titles. This is descriptive chemical knowledge with no handling, inhalation or experiment instruction. Accept solvent-role reading only.

reviewedFor.g8:pure-substances: Every nitrogen atom having seven protons explicitly connects an element identity to proton number.
reviewedFor.g8:count-particles: The number 7 gives a concrete worked identification of proton count from atomic number.

reason: All three bodies retain nitrogen symbol N, atomic number 7 and exactly seven protons; isotope/ion variation does not change that count. Titles align and no emphasis exists. Correct example-level reading, with no neutron/electron count claim.

The floating-equilibrium physics in English/TL is correct, but Cebuano substitutes gitudlo nga tubig for displaced water. Binisaya gives tudlo as point/indicate/teach rather than displacement. That changes the essential quantity in Archimedes' condition. Titles and weight emphasis match, but hold the current Cebuano body before using the balanced-force example.

reviewedFor.g9:e-11: Natural radio emission from stars/galaxies and a radio telescope detecting it give an explicit astronomical research-tool example.

reason: The three bodies distinguish natural sources from human transmitters and retain the radio-telescope instrument. Listen is a familiar signal-detection metaphor here, not a claim that sound travels through space; radio waves are named throughout. Titles and emphasis align. Safe explanatory astronomy reading.

reviewedFor.g7:tsunami-alerts: Names PHIVOLCS as the Philippine earthquake-monitoring and tsunami-warning authority.

reason: The official PHIVOLCS tsunami-information service corroborates the agency role. English/TL/BIS retain monitoring plus warnings when danger exists; titles align and no emphasis exists. Accept official-warning awareness only: this does not tell learners to wait for warnings, nor does it cover natural signs, evacuation or return permission.

English presents higher risk of water/crop impacts, and Cebuano retains peligro, but Tagalog changes that into asserted water shortage and crop damage. PAGASA uses likelihood and regional differences for El Niño rainfall impacts. Hold the certainty increase and unqualified national dry-spell wording; titles are aligned and no emphasis exists.

reviewedFor.g7:fault-models: Stress building across a fault and sudden slip causing an earthquake is the explicit mechanism a fault-motion model illustrates.

reason: English/TL/BIS retain gradual loading followed by sudden slip. TL/BIS use ordinary force language for accumulated fault loading; the text supplies no incorrect force-per-area calculation. Slowly grind is a rough friction metaphor rather than a claim that continuous creep always causes earthquakes. Titles/emphasis align. Accept a qualitative stick-slip example, not a full elastic-rebound model.

reviewedFor.g7:speed-velocity: Explicitly contrasts speed as scalar with velocity as vector using the presence or absence of direction.

reason: All three languages preserve size plus direction for vectors and size alone for scalars; displacement/force and speed/distance examples are correctly assigned. Titles and both emphasis spans match. Direct, safe support for the speed–velocity distinction.

The conductor/insulator contrast is useful, but every body concludes that touching the wire will not shock the child simply because of its plastic coating. Insulation must be intact and suitable; damaged cables or live conductors remain hazardous. TL/BIS make the no-shock assurance particularly categorical. Titles and no-emphasis formatting are aligned, but hold both safety placements until the guarantee is qualified.

The English/BIS extra-CO₂ heat-retention account fits enhanced greenhouse warming, and titles identify trapping heat. Tagalog uses natatabunan ang init, which the corpus otherwise supports as covered/buried material rather than retained outgoing heat. The body does not clarify that metaphor. Hold this unresolved translation of the central mechanism rather than silently substituting the title's nagkukulong sense. No emphasis exists.

reviewedFor.g10:e-3: Locates the Philippine Trench east of the archipelago and Manila Trench to the west near the South China Sea, directly supporting tectonic-map orientation.

reason: English/TL/BIS preserve east/west and distinct plate associations. The card does not name a wrong plate or claim a mapped scale; titles align and no emphasis exists. Accept trench-location reading only, not full map interpretation or mountain/fault/volcano coverage.

The three bodies give generic gloves as a barrier against heat, cuts or chemicals without explaining that different glove materials are selected for different hazards. That omission is consequential in a handling-safety lesson: ordinary laboratory gloves do not safely cover all those hazards. OSHA explicitly ties glove performance to the anticipated hazard. Titles and glove emphasis match; hold until suitable-glove selection is part of the advice.

EN correctly describes radio as electromagnetic radiation, distinct from sound and able to propagate in vacuum; TL preserves that explanation, and the titles and emphasis are aligned. BIS uses makalakaw for propagation through space. Binisaya directly glosses lakaw as walking; the travel entries on that page are broader English semantic relations, not direct attestation of this Cebuano wave-propagation usage. Hold this uncertain lexical choice for native or stronger lexical review, rather than asserting that every figurative use is wrong. The vacuum focus would fit g9:f-10 once the current BIS wording is resolved.

reviewedFor.g9:l-10: The native tindalo example directly connects heavy timber harvesting with a tree becoming rare, providing a concrete Philippine deforestation-impact reading.

reason: All three bodies retain the same limited claim: desirable hard timber has encouraged cutting and contributed to rarity. The EN/TL/BIS tree titles and tindalo emphasis agree. The Palawan Council for Sustainable Development flora survey records Afzelia rhomboidea/tindalo as rare and a construction timber, supporting the species context; the card does not claim endemicity or assign a legal threat category. Suitable supplemental environmental reading, without credit for pollution, invasive species, or source-evaluation tasks.

The current text confuses the broad base of an energy pyramid with a necessarily large number of individual plants: an energy pyramid represents available energy, while organism-number pyramids can have one tree supporting many consumers. Its additional claim that plants supply the starting energy for every other living thing excludes non-plant producers and chemosynthetic food webs. TL and BIS preserve the overgeneralization; their Pyamide titles also contain a spelling defect. Neither g7:trophic-levels nor g7:energy-transfer should receive this current card.

reviewedFor.g8:plant-transport: Evaporation at leaf pores pulling water and dissolved minerals upward from the soil supplies a specific leaf-to-root transport connection for the organs lesson.

reason: EN gives an appropriate short account of transpiration pull; TL and BIS preserve the leaf-pore loss, upward movement, and soil/mineral connection. Suction is a simplified description of tension in the continuous water column, acceptable in this introductory context. Titles accurately identify water leaving leaves, with no emphasis mismatch. The reading supports the coordinated transport pathway without pretending to identify every root/stem structure or explain all transport mechanisms.

All three bodies state an unconditional rule that adding heat makes atoms/molecules vibrate faster and increases their spacing. Added heat during a phase change need not raise temperature, and expansion is not universal for every material and temperature range. Calling all particle motion vibration also leaves the state of matter unspecified. The aligned titles and heat emphasis do not qualify these claims. Hold for g7:particle-motion because the present statement would teach an overgeneralized heat-temperature-spacing relationship.

EN/TL/BIS consistently describe fin removal and population harm, and their titles/emphasis are aligned; the non-graphic conservation topic is age appropriate. The added claim that coral reefs depend on sharks and are therefore harmed as a general consequence is too categorical across shark species and reef contexts. Global reef surveys support fishing-related shark depletion, while primary work on mesopredators describes context-dependent ecological effects. Hold the whole current card rather than approve only its first clause. The threat example would fit g9:l-7, but g9:l-10 also lacks its specific deforestation/pollution/invasive or evidence-evaluation focus.

reviewedFor.g10:f-13: The card directly compares the recurring fuel requirement of fossil-fuel generation with sunlight and wind as renewable energy inputs.

reason: The EN/TL/BIS bodies preserve the operational distinction: coal/oil stations consume purchased fuel, whereas wind turbines and solar panels do not consume such fuel to generate electricity. The daily phrasing is a simple recurring-fuel-cost example, not a procurement schedule to learn. Titles describe the energy inputs as free; the body does not claim that building or maintaining generation equipment costs nothing. Appropriate supplemental comparison, without coverage credit for lifecycle emissions or a complete assessment of energy-source impacts.

All three bodies and their emphasized 38-ATP spans repeat a single unqualified aerobic-respiration yield. That is an older idealized estimate based on particular assumptions, not a reliable general yield for glucose respiration across cells. Contemporary quantitative work and plant bioenergetic analysis show that coupling, transport, and alternative pathways affect ATP yield. ATP molecules also carry usable chemical energy rather than being molecules of energy themselves. Hold g8:photosynthesis-respiration despite the otherwise correct glucose/oxygen and carbon-dioxide/water participants; do not replace one universal number with another.

reviewedFor.g10:f-11: The motor-generator comparison explicitly contrasts electricity-to-motion and motion-to-electricity energy conversion, the central relationship of this lesson.

reason: EN explains a generator by reversing the motor energy conversion; TL and BIS preserve that comparison and the motor/generator titles. Exact opposite is read within the stated conversion direction, not as a claim that every machine design or component is opposite. This is a clear, age-appropriate short comparison; it does not claim to demonstrate electromagnetic induction or cover construction and operation in full. There are no emphasis spans to misalign.

reviewedFor.g7:microscope: Using lens paper on the eyepiece and objective glass gives a concrete microscope-care instruction within the handling focus.

reason: The three bodies retain lens paper, glass surfaces, eyepiece, and objectives without substituting ordinary abrasive paper. The cleaning titles and lens-paper emphasis match their bodies. The order is a reasonable care routine, not a claim that cleaning in another order changes microscope optics. Suitable supervised classroom handling advice and supplemental reading; it supplies neither a full parts/functions lesson nor complete storage instructions.

reviewedFor.g9:e-6: The card introduces eons, eras, and periods, then anchors the relative duration of Precambrian time and the Mesozoic within Earth history.

reason: The three bodies convey the same timescale hierarchy and approximate chronology. Earth at roughly 4.5 billion years and Precambrian time at roughly 88 percent are appropriate rounded figures, and the Mesozoic dinosaur example is correctly located. TL/BIS saying dinosaurs lived there preserves the relevant historical claim without implying that all dinosaur descendants vanished. Titles identify the geologic time scale; no emphasis issue. Useful timeline orientation, not proof that the learner can interpret every boundary or date.

reviewedFor.g7:earthquake-effects: Magnitude, focus depth, epicentral distance, and soft ground provide four explicit factors for comparing shaking experienced by communities.

reason: EN/TL/BIS all distinguish felt intensity from the listed earthquake and site factors, with matching intensity emphasis and appropriate earthquake titles. Larger magnitude, shallower sources, shorter distance, and soft-ground amplification describe the usual comparisons with other conditions comparable; the text does not make the epicenter an unconditional maximum or give a precise local prediction. Accept as explanatory reading for variation in community shaking, not as an earthquake-safety procedure or a quantitative damage model.

The EN and TL bodies give a plausible broad shell-internalization account and correctly compare an ancestral shell with, rather than descend modern cuttlefish from, a nautilus. BIS retains cuttlefish in the body but titles the card Bukog sa Nukos. The consulted dictionary directly glosses nukos as squid; a cuttlefish-specific usage is not established there, and a squid pen is not a cuttlebone. Hold this organism-name uncertainty for native or stronger lexical evidence, rather than trusting a perceived umbrella meaning. The morphology example could support g10:l-5 after resolution. Cuttlebone emphasis is present in every body.

reviewedFor.g7:heat-transfer-uses: A hot-air balloon gives an explicit useful application of heated air rising, suitable as a short convection-context example.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve the warm-air/cool-air comparison and balloon-lift example, and titles/emphasis agree. Lighter is the ordinary equal-volume comparison underlying lower-density heated air in this balloon context; the card is not claiming a fixed mass loses mass when warmed. Accept only the practical rising-air example for g7:heat-transfer-uses. Reject g7:heat-particles: it does not explain particle motion, spacing, or how particle behavior transfers thermal energy.

reviewedFor.g8:periods-groups: Locating metals mainly at the left/center and nonmetals toward the upper right provides a concrete property-based way to read periodic-table regions.

reason: The current EN/TL/BIS titles, bodies, and metal/nonmetal emphasis all agree. The broad regional layout is correct: most metals occupy the left and middle, and nonmetals occur toward the upper right. The wording does not explicitly make that the only nonmetal location; hydrogen remains an exception for the main lesson to explain. Accept as supplemental property-map orientation, without claiming that this card teaches row/column definitions, group numbers, or period counts.

The solar/wind comparison is relevant to g10:e-12, but EN, TL, and BIS all turn low operational emissions into an unqualified claim that this electricity adds no greenhouse gases. The lifecycle assessment dataset separates upstream, operating, and downstream emissions and does not support zero total emissions. The card supplies no operational boundary that would make its absolute wording reliable. The BIS title Solar Wind Gas also drops the reduced/no-emissions relation in the other titles. Hold the current trilingual card; Philippine sunshine alone does not establish a universally perfect generation resource.

reviewedFor.g7:investigation-steps: The conclusion explicitly summarizes findings, checks the investigation aim, and interprets patterns in the collected data, directly supporting the reporting/conclusion step.

reason: EN, TL, and BIS preserve the same data-grounded role for a conclusion. The BIS short sentences improve readability without changing the relationship among findings, aim, and observed patterns; its Konklusyon title and borrowed conclusion emphasis are compatible. The card does not equate an unmet aim with scientific failure or claim every investigation must confirm a prediction. Accept as a clear reporting component, without credit for planning materials, method, or every investigation step.

reviewedFor.g8:subatomic-particles: The card directly compares proton, neutron, and electron charge and places the nuclear particles centrally versus electrons outside the nucleus.

reason: All three versions retain positive proton, neutral neutron, and negative electron charges, with matching particle-name titles and no emphasis spans. The center/outside account is an introductory atomic model and does not specify fixed classical electron tracks. The card describes the usual three particle types, not a numerical assertion that every isotope contains a neutron. Appropriate short comparison for Grade 8; it supplies neither relative masses nor particle symbols.

reviewedFor.g7:litmus: Red in acidic solution and blue in basic solution gives the lesson a direct indicator-color reading.
reviewedFor.g10:m-2: The same specific litmus color responses provide background for interpreting an acid/base indicator test.

reason: EN/TL/BIS give the correct red-acid and blue-base relationship, and the indicator titles and litmus emphasis agree. The color statement is introductory: a strip already displaying the corresponding color need not change again. Nothing here claims litmus uniquely identifies salts or measures an exact pH. Both proposed lessons receive supplemental indicator knowledge only, not an experimental protocol, substance identification, hydrochloric-acid/sodium-hydroxide coverage, or proof that a learner can test unknown solutions safely.

reviewedFor.g7:solar-winds: The card connects stronger daytime land warming, lower pressure over land, and sea-to-shore airflow, directly explaining a sea-breeze example of solar-driven wind.

reason: EN explains daytime land/sea differential warming and the resulting pressure-driven breeze. TL and BIS narrow the scene to midday but preserve its physical mechanism and direction; the air-pressure emphasis and sea-breeze titles remain aligned. NOAA describes the same thermal low over warmed land and cooler surface inflow from water. The simplified pressure chain is suitable supplemental reading, without claiming sea breezes override every weather system or covering monsoons and the ITCZ.

The EN body correctly places replacement-cell mitosis in deeper skin layers; BIS preserves deeper layers and the mitosis title. TL instead says mitosis occurs sa ilalim ng balat, under the skin, changing the anatomical location. The consulted dictionary supports the under/beneath reading, while epidermal-renewal sources place the relevant dividing cells within the epidermis, principally its basal layer. Titles alone do not resolve that body mismatch. Hold g7:cell-division until the TL location is accurate; skin renewal itself is an appropriate and useful growth/repair example.

reviewedFor.g10:l-1: Cold-triggered shivering and heat production by rapid muscle activity give an explicit body-temperature regulation example.

reason: EN/TL/BIS all connect a cold body, rapid muscle activity, and production of heat; their shivering/heat titles match, with no emphasis spans. The explanation is an appropriate short account of muscular thermogenesis, with no treatment advice or unsafe activity instruction. It supports the temperature/homeostasis focus through a concrete response, while leaving the sensor, brain control, and negative-feedback pathway for the main lesson rather than claiming complete homeostasis coverage.

The yearly axial-direction explanation is scientifically acceptable: NASA describes the tilted axis maintaining approximately the same direction during an orbit, with the north axis near Polaris. EN/TL titles and bodies convey that idea, and all tilt emphasis spans match. BIS uses nagaturo for points. A full local root check found ten pointing-context bodies, but these machine-translated repetitions do not establish lexical correctness; Binisaya directly attests tudlo for pointing, while Wolff supplies different meanings for turu. Hold the unresolved Cebuano lexical choice for native or stronger independent evidence, rather than declare a new universal false-friend rule. g7:sunlight-angle would otherwise fit the tilt/orbit focus.

All three bodies and titles preserve the instruction to add two or more batteries in series and the promised much-brighter bulb. Voltages add for correctly oriented sources, but the present instruction gives neither compatible battery/bulb ratings nor a bound on added voltage; a bulb can be overdriven and burn out rather than reliably shine brighter. A primary engineering classroom source confirms excessive filament current can destroy the bulb. The unbounded imperative is unsuitable as a standalone child circuit instruction. Hold g9:f-7 despite the useful underlying series-voltage relationship; no copy repair or substituted activity is authorized.

reviewedFor.g8:kinetic-potential: The same rock at two heights concretely compares gravitational potential energy, and the mass-times-gravity-times-height relation explains why height matters.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve the same-rock comparison and the near-Earth mgh relationship, with height-focused titles.
